from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate", [
            "Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.",
            "Consider a drone moving along a track.",
            "The speedometer reading is its derivative."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        track = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE)
        drone = Dot(self.grid["D1"], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(track), FadeIn(drone))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(drone.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"]), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(drone.animate.move_to(self.grid["D1"]), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        label = MathTex(r"v = \frac{dx}{dt}", color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "C3")
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.play(Circumscribe(drone, color="#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Operation: Accumulation", [
            "Integrals act as the inverse of derivatives.",
            "They accumulate tiny changes over time.",
            "This calculates the total displacement traveled."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**2 + 1, x_range=[0.5, 3.5], color=WHITE)
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 3.5], color="#3385FF", opacity=0.5)
        label = Text("Area = Accumulation", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # Grid setup
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        axes.add(curve, area)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        sweeper = Line(start=axes.c2p(0.5, 0), end=axes.c2p(0.5, 3), color="#FF33A1", stroke_width=4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Write(axes), Create(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Create(area), Write(label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.add(sweeper)
        self.play(sweeper.animate.shift(RIGHT * 3), run_time=3)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweeper))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculus relates these two concepts fundamentally.",
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.",
            "Think of them as reverse operations.",
            "Slice functions into thin rectangles.",
            "Compress them back into slopes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", lecture_lines)

        # Visuals
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*x**2 + 1, x_range=[0, 4], color=WHITE)
        f_prime = MathTex("f'(x)", color="#FF5733")
        integral_sign = MathTex(r"\int", color="#33FF57")
        arrow = Arrow(start=RIGHT, end=LEFT, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)

        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(curve, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(f_prime, 'D5')
        self.place_at_grid(integral_sign, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'D4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(f_prime), FadeIn(integral_sign))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Dummy animation for "Slice functions"
        rects = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=axes.c2p(0, 0.2*x**2+1)[1], width=0.1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for x in range(4)])
        self.play(FadeIn(rects))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(rects))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Real-World Application", [
            "The Fundamental Theorem links these operations.",
            "Integration reconstructs functions from derivatives.",
            "This tool solves real-world physics problems."
        ])
        
        # --- Visual Setup ---
        # Draw a graph
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x + 1, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(axes, graph), 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        total_distance_label = Text("Total Distance", font_size=24, color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(total_distance_label, 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        area = axes.get_area(graph, x_range=[0, 4], color=YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(area, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(Write(total_distance_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate
sections.content: Briefly recall that a derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change (the slope of a tangent line). Visualize a drone flying: the derivative of its position over time is its velocity.
sections.example: A drone moving along a 1D track. At any moment, the speedometer reading is the derivative of its position function.

sections.title: The Inverse Operation: Accumulation
sections.content: Introduce the integral as the 'accumulation' of changes. If the derivative tells us how fast we are changing, the integral adds up all those tiny changes to find the total displacement.
sections.example: If you know the drone's velocity at every moment, integrating that velocity function 'sums up' the tiny distances to show the drone's total change in position.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Visualized)
sections.content: Explain the core relationship: differentiation and integration are inverse processes (like multiplication and division). Show an animation where a function is sliced into thin rectangles (integral) and then compressed back into the slope of a curve (derivative).
sections.example: Think of a 'magic fountain': The rate at which water pours out (derivative) determines the height of the water level in the tank (integral). If you change the pour rate, the water level changes accordingly.

sections.title: Synthesis and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize that F'(x) = f(x) and the integral of f(x) is F(x) + C. Emphasize that the integral 'reconstructs' the function from its rate of change.
sections.example: A smart thermostat: The 'derivative' is the change in room temperature per minute; the 'integral' of that change tells the system the total temperature shift since it was turned on.
